w:r.w:t: The National Research Institute of Maritime Heritage, under the Korea Heritage Service (KHS), announced the discovery of a new Goryeo-period shipwreck, designated Mado No. 6, during underwater excavations off Mado Island in Taean. The institute, headed by
, is currently investigating the newly discovered shipwreck, following
confirmation of Mado No. 5, another shipwreck first detected last year.

Following the discovery of bundles of celadon vessels and fragments of a ship's hull in 2025, which suggested the presence of a fifth shipwreck (Mado No. 5) in the waters off Taean, full-scale underwater excavations began this year. The excavations yielded 5

The wooden tablets recovered from Mado No. 5 bear the inscriptions “Jeongmyo Year” (

), indicating when the cargo was collected. Based on radiocarbon dating of associated organic materials, which places them between the mid-twelfth and early thirteenth centuries, together with the dating of the celadon vessels, researchers have concluded that the Jeongmyo year refers to 1207. The twelfth lunar month of that year corresponds roughly to January 1208 in the Gregorian calendar, when harsh winter conditions would generally have made sea voyages impractical. Mado No. 5 is similar in nature to Mado No. 1, a shipwreck excavated in 2009. Mado No. 1 also sank in 1208 while en route to Gaegyeong, having collected its cargo in 1207. The cargo had been sent from several locations in southwestern Jeolla
, present-day Yeongam). Notably, a wooden tablets (No. 5-20) recovered from
No. 5, identifying a shipment from Anno-hyeon to an individual named Song Deuk-deok (
) in Gaegyeong, is nearly identical in handwriting and content to a wooden tablet (No. 1-34) recovered from
No. 1, also associated with a shipment from Anno-hyeon. Researchers believe the two tablets were written by the same person.

Based on the inscriptions on the wooden tablets, the finds from Mado No. 5 could also be interpreted as belonging to Mado No. 1. However, the two shipwreck sites are approximately 250 meters apart, only some of the locations from which Mado No. 1's cargo was shipped are mentioned on the wooden tablets from Mado No. 5, and the outer hull planking of the two vessels differs. Researchers therefore believe that Mado No. 1 and Mado No. 5 belonged to the same fleet, carrying separate portions of cargo from southwestern Jeolla
Province to Gaegyeong in the spring of 1208. Both ships are thought to have encountered severe weather and sunk in the waters off Mado Island in Taean.

The National Research Institute of Maritime Heritage plans to continue excavations at the Mado No. 5 site in 2027, while focusing on a more extensive investigation of the newly discovered shipwreck believed to have departed from Sacheon in the Gyeongsang

region to establish its nature and historical significance. As Korea's only institution specializing in underwater cultural heritage excavation, the institute will continue its efforts to uncover the nation's submerged cultural heritage and promote greater international awareness of Korea's rich maritime heritage.
